Gianluigi Donnarumma.blurb: Italian giant who broke through at Milan, won Euro 2020 as best player and the 2025 UCL with PSG before joining Manchester City.

Thibaut Courtois.blurb: Towering Belgian keeper for Chelsea, Atlético and Real Madrid, whose man-of-the-match 2022 UCL final display epitomises his big-game shot-stopping.

Alisson.blurb: Brazilian No.1 and Liverpool's mainstay since 2018, a Premier League and 2019 Champions League winner renowned for composure and pinpoint distribution.

Lev Yashin.blurb: Soviet legend the 'Black Spider', the only goalkeeper to win the Ballon d'Or (1963), who redefined the position for Dynamo Moscow and the USSR.

Gianluigi Buffon.blurb: Italy's 2006 World Cup-winning keeper and Juventus icon whose record-length career marks him among the greatest ever.

Iker Casillas.blurb: Spain's captain for the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2008/2012 treble, a Real Madrid icon known as 'San Iker' for reflex saves.

Manuel Neuer.blurb: German 2014 World Cup winner and Bayern mainstay who pioneered the 'sweeper-keeper' role, dominating the space behind a high line.

Oliver Kahn.blurb: Germany's ferociously intense Bayern captain and the only goalkeeper named Player of the Tournament at a World Cup (2002).

Dino Zoff.blurb: Italy's oldest World Cup winner as captain in 1982 at 40, a Juventus great renowned for calm reliability and clean-sheet records.

Peter Schmeichel.blurb: Danish colossus, Euro 1992 winner and Manchester United's treble-winning keeper (1999), famed for his size and the 'star jump' save.

Gordon Banks.blurb: England's 1966 World Cup winner, immortalised by 'the Save of the Century' denying Pelé at the 1970 World Cup.

Edwin van der Sar.blurb: Dutch keeper who starred for Ajax, Fulham and Manchester United, winning the 1995 and 2008 Champions Leagues with a clean-sheet record.

Sepp Maier.blurb: West Germany's 1974 World Cup winner, 'Die Katze von Anzing', a Bayern icon of the 1970s known for agility and reliability.

Achraf Hakimi.blurb: Moroccan right-back for PSG, ex-Real Madrid, Dortmund and Inter; blistering pace, star of Morocco's 2022 World Cup semi-final run.

Dani Carvajal.blurb: Spanish right-back and Real Madrid mainstay, serial Champions League winner; tenacious defending and big-game reliability.

Cafu.blurb: Brazilian right-back, most-capped Brazil player and only man in three straight World Cup finals; tireless 'Il Pendolino' at Roma and Milan.

Roberto Carlos.blurb: Brazilian left-back and 2002 World Cup winner, Real Madrid Galáctico; thunderous free-kicks and an explosive left foot.

Paolo Maldini.blurb: Italian full-back/centre-back, AC Milan one-club legend across 25 seasons; the gold standard of positional, clean-tackling defence.

Philipp Lahm.blurb: German full-back for both sides, Bayern and Germany captain and 2014 World Cup winner; cerebral, two-footed defending.

Javier Zanetti.blurb: Argentine full-back/midfielder and Inter captain over 19 seasons; extraordinary durability and versatility, 2010 treble winner.

Dani Alves.blurb: Brazilian right-back, the most decorated player in football history; Barcelona's overlapping partner to Messi in the tiki-taka era.

Carlos Alberto.blurb: Brazilian right-back and captain of the 1970 World Cup winners; scorer of that final's iconic team goal, an attacking full-back pioneer.

Ashley Cole.blurb: English left-back for Arsenal's 'Invincibles' and Chelsea; among the best defensive full-backs, master of nullifying elite wingers.

Nílton Santos.blurb: Brazilian left-back, Botafogo legend and 1958/1962 World Cup winner; the 'Enciclopédia do Futebol' who pioneered the attacking full-back.

Gary Neville.blurb: English right-back and Manchester United one-club man, Class of '92; dependable defending and a legendary partnership with Beckham.

Virgil van Dijk.blurb: Dutch colossus and Liverpool captain, the record signing who transformed their defence and finished 2nd in the 2019 Ballon d'Or.

Rúben Dias.blurb: Portuguese leader signed by Man City in 2020; immediately won the title and FWA Footballer of the Year for organising the backline.

Antonio Rüdiger.blurb: German warrior who won the 2021 UCL with Chelsea before anchoring Real Madrid's defence, famed for relentless aggression.

Franz Beckenbauer.blurb: German legend 'Der Kaiser' who invented the attacking libero at Bayern, won the 1974 World Cup as captain and two Ballons d'Or.

Franco Baresi.blurb: Italian AC Milan one-club icon and libero who marshalled Sacchi's dynasty and the world's most feared offside trap.

Fabio Cannavaro.blurb: Italian captain who won the 2006 World Cup and became the only defender to win the Ballon d'Or that year.

Alessandro Nesta.blurb: Italian centre-back regarded as the most technically elegant defender ever, a Lazio and AC Milan great with two UCL titles.

Sergio Ramos.blurb: Spanish serial winner and Real Madrid captain, a four-time UCL winner famed for clutch goals like the 2014 final equaliser.

Bobby Moore.blurb: England's 1966 World Cup-winning captain and West Ham legend, revered for immaculate timing and positioning despite lacking pace.

Carles Puyol.blurb: Spanish Barcelona one-club captain and heart of the 2008–2011 dynasty, a tenacious leader and 2010 World Cup winner.

Rio Ferdinand.blurb: English ball-playing centre-back and Man United great, six-time PL champion and 2008 UCL winner known for pace and elegant passing.

Daniel Passarella.blurb: Argentine 1978 World Cup-winning captain 'El Gran Capitán', a River Plate legend and highest-scoring defender of his era.

Pedri.blurb: Spanish creative midfielder, Barcelona and Spain's tempo-setter, celebrated for press resistance and mature ball retention.

Jude Bellingham.blurb: English box-to-box midfielder who starred at Dortmund then Real Madrid, known for late runs, big-game goals and precocious leadership.

Zinedine Zidane.blurb: French maestro, star of Juventus and Real Madrid and 1998 World Cup winner, revered for elegant control and the 2002 UCL final volley.

Xavi Hernández.blurb: Spanish deep-lying playmaker, Barcelona's tiki-taka metronome and a Spain treble winner who defined possession football.

Andrés Iniesta.blurb: Spanish playmaker, Barcelona icon and scorer of Spain's 2010 World Cup-winning goal, famed for gliding dribbles through defences.

Michel Platini.blurb: French attacking midfielder, three-time Ballon d'Or winner with Juventus, a prolific scoring playmaker and Euro 1984 talisman.

Andrea Pirlo.blurb: Italian deep-lying playmaker, regista at Milan and Juventus and 2006 World Cup winner who redefined the role.

Steven Gerrard.blurb: English box-to-box midfielder and one-club Liverpool captain, driver of the 2005 Istanbul comeback, famed for powerful shooting.

Paul Scholes.blurb: English central midfielder and Manchester United one-club great, revered by peers for passing range, timing of runs and goals from deep.

Lothar Matthäus.blurb: German midfielder, 1990 World Cup-winning captain and inaugural FIFA World Player, a commanding box-to-box force at Bayern and Inter.

Frank Rijkaard.blurb: Dutch midfielder, part of Milan's and Ajax's late-80s greats and a 1988 Euro winner, an elegant, versatile all-rounder.

Roy Keane.blurb: Irish combative midfielder and Manchester United captain of the 1999 treble, a fierce leader defining their late-90s dominance.

Vinícius Júnior.blurb: Brazilian left winger for Real Madrid, breakout star of the 2020s who scored the winner in the 2022 UCL final and drives Madrid's attack.

Mohamed Salah.blurb: Egyptian right winger and Liverpool talisman, multiple Premier League Golden Boots, famous for cutting inside onto his left foot.

Garrincha.blurb: Brazilian right winger of Botafogo, 'Little Bird', two-time World Cup winner who mesmerised despite bent legs from childhood illness.

George Best.blurb: Northern Irish winger for Manchester United, 1968 European Cup winner and Ballon d'Or holder, as famous off the pitch as on it.

Cristiano Ronaldo.blurb: Portuguese superstar who began as a stepover winger at Man United before becoming a prolific scorer at Real Madrid, Juventus and Al-Nassr.

Lionel Messi.blurb: Argentine maestro, Barcelona icon and 2022 World Cup winner who from a right-wing base redefined the false-nine with peerless dribbling.

Ronaldinho.blurb: Brazilian playmaking winger, 2005 Ballon d'Or winner at Barcelona, the embodiment of joyful football with samba tricks and no-look passes.

Ryan Giggs.blurb: Welsh left winger, one-club legend at Manchester United with record longevity and 13 titles, famed for mazy solo goals.

Stanley Matthews.blurb: English right winger, the 'Wizard of Dribble', first Ballon d'Or winner (1956) and 1953 FA Cup hero who played top-flight football until 50.

Luís Figo.blurb: Portuguese winger, 2000 Ballon d'Or winner, notorious for his transfer from Barcelona to Real Madrid, a master of crossing and dribbling.

Arjen Robben.blurb: Dutch right winger for Chelsea, Real Madrid and Bayern, scorer of the 2013 UCL final winner, famous for cutting inside onto his left foot.

Franck Ribéry.blurb: French left winger and Bayern icon, driving force of the 2013 treble, a dazzling dribbler who formed the 'Robbery' duo with Robben.

Kylian Mbappé.blurb: French superstar and 2018 World Cup winner, PSG's record scorer before Real Madrid; hat-trick in the 2022 World Cup final.

Ousmane Dembélé.blurb: French winger/forward, ex-Barcelona now PSG, who won the 2025 UCL and Ballon d'Or, an ambidextrous dribbler of rare unpredictability.

Erling Haaland.blurb: Norwegian goal-machine at Manchester City (via Salzburg/Dortmund); broke the single-season Premier League record with 36 goals in 2022-23.

Pelé.blurb: Brazilian icon and only three-time World Cup winner (1958, 62, 70); Santos legend widely regarded among the greatest ever, ~1000+ goals.

Ronaldo Nazário.blurb: Brazilian 'O Fenômeno', two-time World Cup winner and 2002 Golden Boot; unstoppable at Barcelona, Inter and Real Madrid before injuries.

Marco van Basten.blurb: Dutch elegant No.9, three-time Ballon d'Or winner at AC Milan and Euro 88 champion with a legendary volley; retired at 30 to injury.

Gerd Müller.blurb: German 'Der Bomber', Bayern and West Germany legend who won the 1974 World Cup and set scoring records unmatched for decades.

Alfredo Di Stéfano.blurb: Argentine-Spanish all-round forward who drove Real Madrid to five straight European Cups (1956–60), scoring in all five finals.

Romário.blurb: Brazilian poacher and 1994 World Cup winner/Golden Ball; Barcelona and Brazil legend with cold-blooded finishing and 1000+ career goals.

Gabriel Batistuta.blurb: Argentine 'Batigol', Fiorentina icon and their all-time top scorer; a ferocious striker who finally won Serie A at Roma in 2001.

Thierry Henry.blurb: French World Cup winner and Arsenal's record scorer / 'Invincibles' talisman; a converted winger who became a lethal, elegant striker.

Ruud van Nistelrooy.blurb: Dutch penalty-box predator, prolific for Man United and Real Madrid in the 2000s; a pure poacher with relentless records.

Eusébio.blurb: Portuguese 'Black Panther', Benfica legend and 1966 World Cup top scorer (9 goals) with a European Cup and 1965 Ballon d'Or.

Dídac Plana.blurb: Spanish goalkeeper for Barça and Spain, a league and Copa winner famed for spectacular reflex saves and commanding his area.

Luis Amado.blurb: Spanish goalkeeper legend of Inter Movistar and Spain, a World Cup (2000, 2004) and multiple Euro winner famed for consistency and command of his box.

Stefano Mammarella.blurb: Italian goalkeeper and Italy's Euro 2014-winning keeper, named that tournament's best; known for reflexes and leadership.

Higuita.blurb: Same player as Léo Higuita — the Brazilian-born fly-goalkeeper (nicknamed after René Higuita) who dribbles and scores from his own goal.

Guitta.blurb: Brazilian goalkeeper for Corinthians/Magnus and Brazil, a Futsal Planet World's Best Goalkeeper (2021) known for lightning reflexes and elite 1v1 shot-stopping.

Tomás Paçó.blurb: Young Portuguese fixo at Sporting CP and a Portugal international, a composed ball-playing defender in the 2021 World Cup-winning squad.

Kike Boned.blurb: Spanish fixo (Enrique Boned) and ElPozo Murcia icon; 2× World champion (2000, 2004) and 2009 World Player, a cerebral defender.

Pany Varela.blurb: Cape Verde-born Portuguese winger (Benfica) who scored in the 2021 Champions League and World Cup finals for Portugal.

Ricardinho.blurb: Portuguese winger No.10 'O Mágico', a record 6× Futsal Planet World Player who captained Portugal to the 2021 World Cup (Golden Ball).

Falcão.blurb: Brazilian icon dubbed the 'Pelé of futsal'; 2× World Cup winner (2008, 2012), 4× World Player, with 400+ goals for Brazil.

Manoel Tobias.blurb: Brazilian legend, 2× World Cup winner and 3× Best Player in the World; considered by many the greatest futsal player ever.

Zicky Té.blurb: Guinea-Bissau-born Portuguese pivot for Sporting CP and Portugal; named 2022 Best Young Player in the World.

Ferrão.blurb: Brazilian pivot and multiple Best Player in the World winner; Barcelona's talisman 2014–24 and a world champion.

Vander Carioca.blurb: Brazilian pivot with one of the longest careers in the sport; World Cup squads 2000 and 2004, still playing into his 40s.

Wilde.blurb: Brazilian pivot and 2× World Cup winner (2008, 2012); multiple Spanish league titles as a powerful target player.

Lenísio.blurb: Brazilian pivot/forward and prolific marksman; multiple LNFS and Brazilian league top scorer, netting 11 at the 2008 World Cup.
